sentences.text: Opposite Party :- The State Of U.P. Thru.
The Prin. Secy. Deptt. Of Home, Lko.

And Other
Counsel for Applicant :- Sachin Srivastava
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Pankaj Bhatia,J.
1. Heard learned counsel for the applicant as well as learned A.G.A. and perused the record.
None appears for the complainant despite notice.
2. In terms of the FIR, a missing person report was lodged alleging
that applicant along with his family members had enticed away the daughter of the victim.

Subsequently, in the statement under Section 161 Cr.P.C., the victim did not support the prosecution version and stated that she wanted to marry the applicant and thereafter physical relations were also formed.
There is a slight variance in the statement under Section 164 Cr.P.C., however, she admitted that the applicant had promised to marry her and she had gone along with the applicant.

sentences.text: 3. In view of the said, the submission of the counsel for the applicant is that applicant should be enlarged on bail.
4. Learned A.G.A. opposed the bail prayer by arguing that as per the certificate of the CMO, the tentative age of the victim is 15-16 years, thus the bail application should be rejected.

5. Considering the submissions prima facie in the statement under section 161 & 164 Cr.P.C., the victim has not supported the prosecution story and stated that she had gone with the applicant voluntarily.

As regards the age of the victim, there is no document on record as prescribed under the Juvenile Justice Act and the Rules framed thereunder to determine the age of the victim at this stage, which shall be considered during trial.

6. Considering the said two statements of the victim recorded under section 161 & 164 Cr.P.C.,
wherein she did not support the prosecution version coupled with the fact that the applicant has no criminal history and is in custody since 09.06.2023 and there is nothing on record to demonstrate that the applicant if enlarged on bail, would in any way adversely affect the trial and without expressing any opinion on merit, I am of the view that the applicant is entitled to be released on bail.
Accordingly, the bail application is allowed.

7. Let the applicant Siraj Mohammad, be released on bail in FIR/ Case Crime No. 71 of 2023, under Sections 147, 363, 366, 370, 323, 504, 506, 376 IPC, Section 3(2)(v) SC/ST Act and Section 3/4 POCSO Act, Police Station Sujauli, District Bahraich, on his furnishing personal bonds and two reliable sureties of Rs.25,000/- each to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions:
(a) The applicant shall execute a bond to undertake to attend the hearings;
(b) The applicant shall not commit any offence similar to the offence of which he is accused or suspected of the commission; and (c) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
Order Date :- 17.1.2024 Arun  Siraj Mohammad vs The State Of U.P. Thru.
